candidates.exact_span: \1 It is advised that the influent and effluent samples are collected considering flow detention time through each plant. Analytical MQLs should be used so that the data can also be used for Local Limits assessment and NPDES application purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of this advisory sampling and MQL guidance as an enforceable monitoring obligation versus non-binding advice can change whether monitoring was required (B), whether reported values are usable for limit comparison (A), and how missing or below-MQL results are classified when evidence is absent (C).

candidates.exact_span: \2 Maximum Allowable Headworks Loading limitation in ug/l. Only complete for pollutants that have approved Technically Based Local Limits.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The completeness condition and stated units determine whether a numeric headworks loading limit is enforceable for a given pollutant (A) and whether absence of an approved local limit leaves applicability or missing-evidence status unresolved rather than supporting a compliance comparison (C).

candidates.exact_span: \3 Daily average effluent limit in the NPDES permit OR the applicable state Water Quality Standard calculated to an equivalent permit effluent limit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The disjunctive source of the daily average effluent limit—permit text versus a WQS-derived equivalent—determines which numeric limit applies when both could be read as candidates, changing exceedance evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: \4 Record names of any pollutants [40 CFR 122, Appendix D, Table II and/or Table V] detected and the quantity in which they were detected.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this recording requirement applies to a given monitoring context affects whether monitoring or reporting was required when pollutants are detected (B) and whether missing pollutant-name or quantity records represent adequate evidence, a documented no-data state, or unresolved missing evidence (C).
